sections.h2: Which offices deal with a Whitley County, Kentucky tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work. The valuation administrator, known as the PVA, sets each parcel's value, the sheriff mails and collects the bill, and the county clerk handles whatever is still open in spring. The fiscal court's directory lists Property Valuation at (606) 549-6008 or 6009 and the sheriff at (606) 549-6006 or 6007. County offices share the courthouse at 200 Main Street, Williamsburg, and the sheriff's site has a bill lookup.

Whitley covers 445 square miles of the Cumberland Plateau, with elevations from 723 to 2,220 feet. The Laurel and Cumberland rivers cross it, roughly 38,000 acres of the west belong to the Daniel Boone National Forest, and Cumberland Falls, Kentucky's largest waterfall, drops inside its borders. Williamsburg is the seat and Corbin is the biggest city, reaching into Knox and Laurel counties. Williamsburg Independent runs a single K-12 school, Corbin Independent crosses county lines, and Whitley County Schools covers the rest.

sections.h2: What is the housing market like in Whitley County?
sections.html:
Prices are low. Five year American Community Survey numbers for 2020 through 2024 value the middle owned home at $131,800, while the typical household brings in $44,615 a year. Roughly two of every three households own where they live.

  • Housing units on the July 2025 count: 15,904.
  • Typical rent: $798 a month.
  • Monthly costs for owners: $1,156 with a mortgage, $346 without.
  • Permits for new homes in 2025: only 52.
  • Residents under the poverty line: 25.5 percent.

Coal and timber built the county's economy, and the 1883 railroad spur helped both grow. The 2022 business census counted $493.3 million of receipts in the health care sector, close to the $526.5 million of retail sales. The University of the Cumberlands is in Williamsburg, and Eastern Kentucky University runs a branch campus near Woodbine. The population reached 37,297 in the 2025 estimate, 1.6 percent above the 2020 count.

sections.h2: What is Whitley County's history and daily life like?
sections.html:
Whitley was carved out of Knox County on January 17, 1818, and named for pioneer William Whitley. McCreary County was split off in 1912, and the courthouse burned in 1931 before federal money paid for a new one. North Corbin has the cafe where KFC began in 1930. Corbin and Williamsburg are the two places with retail alcohol sales, and the county is otherwise classed as moist.

Population swings tell the story of coal and timber. The count reached 31,982 in 1910, slid to 24,145 by 1970, then jumped to 33,396 in 1980 and stood at 36,712 in 2020. The median age that year was 38.0, with 24.3 percent of residents under 18 and 17.0 percent at least 65. The census counted 13,794 households and 15,469 housing units, 10.8 percent of them vacant. Rural areas hold 63.7 percent of the population.

Newer survey figures show 83.3 percent of households with broadband, 20.9 percent of adults with a bachelor's degree, 1,124 veterans and a mean commute of 24.5 minutes. In 2023 the county had 629 employer establishments with 10,058 jobs and a payroll of $466.4 million. Williamsburg-Whitley County Airport is the county's airfield.

sections.h2: How does a Whitley County bill escalate if it is not paid?
sections.html:
The state schedule in KRS 134.015 runs from a 2 percent discount by November 1 to a 10 percent penalty after January. Whoever owned the house on January 1 owes that year's bill personally, so a spring closing does not erase it.

If the sheriff has not been paid by April 15, the bill goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien. From then on 1 percent interest accrues monthly, the clerk adds 10 percent and the county attorney adds 20 percent. The lien follows the parcel for up to 11 years, whoever buys it.

Whitley's clerk then sells the debt to private buyers. Terms for the 2025 bills are in the table.

sections.h2: How do you contest a Whitley County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet the PVA first, since Kentucky bars an appeal without that meeting. Values are fixed as of January 1, the roll opens to the public on the first Monday of May for 13 days, and the meeting belongs inside that window.

Then file with the County Clerk by the end of the next workday. A local board hears the case 25 to 35 days later and dismisses anything that comes without proof.

  • Recent sales of nearby houses like yours.
  • Photos and repair quotes where the house has defects the record misses.
  • Insurance or construction cost papers.

Before you file, ask which sales the PVA used on your parcel.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the homestead exemption in Whitley County?
sections.html: Homeowners at least 65 years old, and the totally disabled, subtract a fixed amount from the assessed value of the home they live in. A couple gets one deduction. File form 62A350 at the PVA office; an approved claim carries forward while the same owner stays. A buyer must apply again, and the PVA can quote the current deduction, which the state resets every two years.

sections.h2: What should a Whitley County seller confirm before closing?
sections.html:
Treat the tax like a payoff, alongside any mortgage. The title company asks the sheriff and the clerk for balances, and both come out of what you receive.

  • Match the name on the bill to the deed.
  • Look for a bill on a garage, mobile home or other addition missing from earlier rolls.
  • On an inherited house, check whether the bill was mailed to someone who has died.
  • Ask the clerk if an earlier year was sold to a private buyer.

Get each balance in writing so the payoff matches the closing statement.

faqs.q: Where does a Whitley County owner send the tax payment?
faqs.a: To the sheriff, whose site offers an online lookup and whose office the fiscal court lists at (606) 549-6006 or 6007. After April 15 the bill sits with the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Is it too late to pay a Whitley County bill after January?
faqs.a: No, but the cost rises. A 10 percent penalty applies after January, and after April 15 monthly interest and commissions come on top.

faqs.q: Can a Whitley County owner sell with a delinquent bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company gets the figures from the sheriff and clerk, and the balance is subtracted from what you receive. The lien stays until it is cleared.

faqs.q: When must a Whitley County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: By the end of the workday after the roll inspection ends. The roll opens the first Monday of May for 13 days, and you must meet the PVA before filing.

faqs.q: Which Whitley County office answers valuation questions?
faqs.a: Property Valuation, listed at (606) 549-6008 or 6009. The sheriff covers the amount due, and the clerk covers delinquent bills.
